question: Which of the following is a distinguishing feature of India’s textile sector?

options.text: It is self-sufficient across the full value chain
It caters solely to domestic markets

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is self-sufficient across the full value chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's textile sector** is unique because it is **self-sufficient across the full value chain**, from the production of raw materials such as cotton, jute, and silk to the manufacturing of finished goods like apparel and home textiles.
 
• India is one of the largest producers of **cotton, jute, and silk** globally, and it has a robust infrastructure supporting spinning, weaving, dyeing, and finishing processes.
 
• The sector is **vertically integrated**, meaning it can handle every stage of production domestically without relying significantly on imports. This makes it resilient and competitive in global markets. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• Unlike other countries that might focus solely on raw materials or finished products, India’s textile industry covers everything from **fiber production** to **value-added exports** such as designer garments and technical textiles.
 
• Statements 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect because the Indian textile sector does not export only raw materials (as it exports finished goods extensively), does not rely on importing finished products (due to its self-sufficiency), and caters to both domestic and international markets rather than solely focusing on domestic consumption. *Hence, statement 3 is the distinguishing feature.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of India’s Textile Sector:**

 
 
• **Age:** The textile industry in India is one of the oldest industries, dating back centuries. It has a long tradition of producing high-quality fabrics like silk and cotton.
 
• **Location:** Major textile hubs include **Tiruppur (Tamil Nadu), Surat (Gujarat), Ludhiana (Punjab), and Mumbai (Maharashtra).**
 
• **Exports:** India is a major exporter of textiles and garments to countries like the **USA, UK, UAE, and Germany**. It contributes significantly to global textile trade.
 
• **Employment:** The textile industry is the **second-largest employer** in India, providing jobs to millions of people directly and indirectly.
 
• **Government Support:** The government has introduced initiatives such as the **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme**, **Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS)**, and **National Technical Textiles Mission** to boost the sector.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** India does not export only raw materials. It exports a significant amount of finished products, including garments, technical textiles, and home furnishings.
 
• **Option 2:** India does not import most of its finished products. Its self-sufficient infrastructure ensures that it produces most finished goods domestically.
 
• **Option 4:** India’s textile industry caters to both **domestic and international markets**. It is not limited to domestic consumption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Ranking:** India is the **second-largest textile and garment producer** globally, second only to China.
 
• **Technical Textiles:** India is increasingly investing in **technical textiles**, which are used in industries like healthcare, construction, and automotive.
 
• **Challenges:** Despite its strengths, the sector faces challenges such as **high input costs, stiff competition from China, and fluctuating demand** in global markets.
 
• **Opportunities:** Initiatives like **‘Make in India’** and increasing demand for sustainable and eco-friendly textiles offer immense growth opportunities for the sector.
